9	# ADR-008: Service Package and Transcript Boundaries
10	
11	| Date | Status | Deciders | Related | Confidence |
12	|------|--------|----------|---------|------------|
13	| 2026-05-05 | Accepted | Fizeau maintainers | `CONTRACT-003`, `ADR-005`, `ADR-006` | High |
14	
15	## Context
16	
17	The repository root is the public Go package:
18	
19	```go
20	github.com/easel/fizeau
21	```
22	
23	That package is currently carrying more than the public contract. It contains
24	the exported service API, concrete service execution, routing/status support,
25	provider quota state, transcript/progress rendering, session-log mechanics,
26	test seams, and a large test surface. This makes the package hard to reason
27	about and makes downstream consumers more likely to treat implementation
28	details as public behavior.
29	
30	The same boundary problem exists at runtime. Fizeau owns native providers and
31	subprocess harness adapters, but downstream consumers such as DDx have grown
32	compensating code that parses harness-native streams, tails Fizeau session-log
33	files, renders human progress lines, and infers runtime status from internal
34	telemetry. That duplicates Fizeau concerns and creates drift between harnesses.
35	
36	Pure no-op compactions are already silent in the agent loop: when the compactor
37	returns the no-op signal, Fizeau emits no compaction start/end event. Any
38	downstream policy that watches for repeated no-op compaction telemetry is
39	therefore observing a stale or invalid signal.
40	
41	## Decision
42	
43	### 1. Root package is the public facade
44	
45	The root `package fizeau` is the compatibility boundary for external
46	consumers. It should contain exported service interfaces, request/response
47	types, event types, constructors, errors, compatibility aliases when needed,
48	and public contract tests.
49	
50	Concrete service implementation code should move behind internal packages.
51	The likely end state is:
52	
53	```text
54	internal/serviceimpl
55	internal/transcript
56	internal/routehealth
57	internal/quota
58	```
59	
60	This follows the official Go module layout guidance: an importable library
61	package can live at the module root, commands live under `cmd/`, and private
62	implementation packages live under `internal/`. This is a package-boundary
63	change, not a module split. The module import path stays stable as
64	`github.com/easel/fizeau`.
65	
66	Do not create a nested `fizeau/` package under this module. With the existing
67	module path, that would either create the stutter import path
68	`github.com/easel/fizeau/fizeau` or force the repository into a
69	nested-module/workspace shape. Neither tradeoff is justified by this decision.
70	Introducing additional `go.mod` modules is deferred until the internal
71	boundaries have proven stable and a real multi-module need exists.
72	
73	### 2. Public service types stay public
74	
75	Public contract types should remain in the root package unless there is a
76	separate, deliberate decision to create a public subpackage. Root aliases to
77	an `internal` package are avoided because they make API identity and
78	documentation harder to understand and can leak unimportable implementation
79	paths into tooling.
80	
81	Internal packages may depend on root public types only through narrow seams
82	that avoid import cycles. If an implementation move exposes a cycle, the fix
83	is to introduce smaller implementation-local interfaces or adapter functions,
84	not to make the root package absorb implementation code again.
85	
86	### 3. Fizeau owns transcript and progress semantics
87	
88	Fizeau is the owner of:
89	
90	- harness-native stream parsing;
91	- native-provider event normalization;
92	- public service event construction;
93	- tool call/result pairing;
94	- payload-size accounting;
95	- compact progress/status line rendering;
96	- session-log lifecycle and replay projections.
97	
98	The canonical human-readable live line is the Fizeau-owned progress payload,
99	currently `ServiceProgressData.Message`. It must remain bounded and suitable
100	for downstream display without downstream parsing of prompts, tool input, tool
101	output, or harness-native JSON.
102	
103	Harnesses may differ internally, but once an interaction crosses the
104	`FizeauService` boundary, downstream consumers should see the same public event
105	vocabulary and required fields.
106	
107	### 4. Downstream consumers are pass-through clients
108	
109	DDx and other consumers may:
110	
111	- call public `FizeauService` methods;
112	- forward or store public `ServiceEvent` values;
113	- display Fizeau-provided progress text;
114	- link or copy Fizeau-owned session artifacts;
115	- decode final/routing fields needed for their own bookkeeping.
116	
117	They must not:
118	
119	- parse harness-native streams such as Claude `stream-json`;
120	- synthesize Fizeau internal session events;
121	- tail and render Fizeau session-log JSONL as policy input;
122	- reconstruct tool transcripts for routing/retry decisions;
123	- infer runtime failure from private or historical Fizeau telemetry.
124	
125	DDx still owns its own bead/worker lifecycle events: bead claimed, attempt
126	started, review running, landed, preserved, failed, and similar outer workflow
127	state. Those events are separate from Fizeau's agent transcript.
128	
129	### 5. No-op compaction is silent
130	
131	Pure no-op compaction probes are not progress and are not telemetry for
132	downstream policy. They remain silent at the public service boundary. Real
133	compaction work and real compaction failures remain Fizeau runtime concerns.
134	
135	Any stale API or downstream code that models a no-op compaction stall breaker
136	must be removed in follow-on implementation beads.
137	
138	## Consequences
139	
140	- The root package becomes smaller and easier to audit for public API
141	  compatibility.
142	- Implementation tests move with the packages that own the behavior.
143	- Transcript rendering becomes consistent across native, Claude, Codex,
144	  Gemini, Pi, and Opencode paths.
145	- DDx changes are blocked until Fizeau ships the public surface needed for
146	  pass-through consumption.
147	- Some refactors will be mechanically large; each implementation bead must
148	  keep source compatibility and run `go test ./...`.
149	
150	## Implementation Implications
151	
152	1. Delete stale no-op compaction stall policy from Fizeau.
153	2. Move concrete service implementation behind `internal/serviceimpl`.
154	3. Introduce `internal/transcript` for public event/progress construction.
